title: Project audit
description: Coordinate a review-only project audit with nine core specialists and research when relevant.
intent: Assess the requested project or bounded subsystem against its accepted goals and available evidence. Report findings; do not apply source fixes by default.

assignments.task: Map accepted requirements, implementation states, critical paths, and readiness gates; provide the scoped evidence brief for subsequent reviewers.
Gather current authoritative references needed to assess the requested audit scope; return sources for subsequent domain and evidence checks.
assignments.when: The audit requires external/current guidance, compatibility facts, or source-backed comparisons.

assignments.task: Review implementation fit, owning boundaries, compatibility, and feasibility of proposed repairs without editing source.
Review relevant architecture, ownership, failure paths, and accepted structural decisions.
Review product fit, design-system usage, representative UI states, and accessibility evidence; mark unavailable visual checks unverified.
Review correctness, meaningful test coverage, flakiness, robustness, and relevant actual check results.
Review reachable security weaknesses and controls using source or authorized isolated validation.
Assess available performance evidence and critical-path costs with existing scoped tooling; avoid mandatory new benchmark harnesses or unauthorized load.
Validate provenance, reproducibility, uncertainty, and whether project/finding claims are supported.
Review relevant artifact, compatibility, deployment, and recovery gates; do not tag, publish, or deploy.

completion: All nine core assignments and any applicable research assignment return actual results or explicit blocked/failed status; none is silently omitted.
Duplicate root causes and contradictory findings are reconciled with source evidence.
The final report distinguishes verified findings, heuristic risks, and unverified readiness gates.
